extracted.intended_audience: applicants/petitioners (inventors, patent attorneys/agents) seeking revival of an unintentionally abandoned U.S. patent application
extracted.subtask_description: Completing and submitting a petition to the USPTO Office of Petitions to revive a patent application abandoned unintentionally under 37 CFR 1.137(a), including required fees, statements, and supporting documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition fee (required)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition fee under 37 CFR 1.17(m)(1) or (m)(2) must be paid for a petition to revive an unintentionally abandoned application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee amount depends on whether delay is greater than two years or less than or equal to two years, and on entity status (other than small/micro, small entity, micro entity). Fee codes are provided (e.g., 1468/2468/3468 for >2 years; 1453/2453/3453 for <=2 years). Include appropriate fee payment with the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper fee selection by delay-length and entity status
rubrics_metrics.description: Select and pay the correct fee based on (a) whether the delay is greater than two years or less than or equal to two years, and (b) the applicant's entity status (other than small, small, or micro).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must assert small entity status per 37 CFR 1.27 or micro entity per 37 CFR 1.29 and provide required documentation (Form PTO/SB/15A or B or equivalent for micro entities). Use the corresponding fee code for the chosen category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply and/or issue fee (required if applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reply to the Office notice/action and/or the issue/publication fee (if applicable) for the underlying Office notice must be filed or paid as part of the petition process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate the type of reply and whether it has been filed previously or is enclosed. If issue/publication fee has been paid previously, provide the date; otherwise enclose payment. Ensure the reply satisfies the Office notice that caused abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer (if required) and disclaimer fee
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer (and disclaimer fee per 37 CFR 1.20(d)) is required for certain applications and must be included when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminal disclaimer is required for all utility and plant applications filed before June 8, 1995, and for all design applications. For utility/plant applications filed on/after June 8, 1995, no terminal disclaimer is required. If applicable, include the terminal disclaimer (see PTO/SB/63) and the disclaimer fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement that the entire delay was unintentional (required)
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must state that the entire delay in filing the required reply until filing the petition under 37 CFR 1.137(a) was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement is mandatory for a grantable petition. The form provides examples of delays that are not considered unintentional (deliberate courses of action), e.g., choosing not to file because claims are not considered patentable, not worth the expense, or to defer fees—such intentional decisions do not qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional explanation for petitions filed more than two years after abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petition is filed more than two years after the date the application became abandoned, an additional explanation of the circumstances is required to establish that the entire delay was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This additional information is required in addition to the unintentionality statement (see 85 FR 12222 (March 2, 2020) and MPEP 711.03(c)(II)(C)-(F)). If this box/option is checked, section 1A must also be completed and supporting statements or documentation should be enclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and computation of abandonment date
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of abandonment is the day after the expiration date of the period set for reply in the Office notice or action plus any extensions of time actually obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition to determine whether the petition is filed within two years or later, which affects fee category and the need for additional explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition/anti-patterns: deliberate courses of action are not unintentional
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliberate choices by the applicant (e.g., not filing because claims are not patentable or to defer fees) do not constitute an 'unintentional' delay and will not make the petition grantable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner is reminded that the correctness of Office rejections, decisions, or subsequent discovery of new information does not retroactively make a deliberate abandonment unintentional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must be signed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.33, and signature requirements under 37 CFR 1.4(d) must be followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include signature, date, typed/printed name, registration number if applicable, telephone number, and address. Submit multiple forms if more than one signature is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of mailing or transmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a Certificate of Mailing or Transmission (37 CFR 1.8(a)) showing the date and method of deposit/transmission to the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable evidence: deposit with the U.S. Postal Service as first-class mail addressed to Mail Stop Petition, Commissioner for Patents (include date), or transmission via USPTO patent electronic filing system or by facsimile (include date and fax number (571) 273-8300). Include signature and typed/printed name of person signing the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enclosures checklist (required supporting items)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure required enclosures accompany the petition: petition fee, reply and/or fee, terminal disclaimer form (if applicable), additional sheets with statements establishing unintentional delay, and any other supporting documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of typical enclosures appears on the form; failure to include required enclosures may prevent grant of the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity-status documentation for micro entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Micro entity applicants must enclose Form PTO/SB/15A or B or equivalent to establish micro entity status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Micro-entity fee codes apply only if the appropriate form or equivalent has been enclosed or previously submitted. Small-entity assertions are governed by 37 CFR 1.27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid submission of unnecessary personal information
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include sensitive personal information (e.g., social security numbers, bank account numbers, credit card numbers) except required payment authorization forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal information in the application file may become public after publication or issuance; redact such information before submission. Checks and credit card authorization forms (PTO-2038) submitted for payment are not retained in the application file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where and how to submit the petition / contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission instructions: mail to Commissioner for Patents, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313-1450; fax to (571) 273-8300; or use the USPTO patent electronic filing system. Contact Office of Petitions for assistance at (571) 272-3282 or 1-800-PTO-9199 (option 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send fees or completed forms to the Privacy Act mailing address listed for comments on the information collection burden. Follow mailing/transmission instructions on the form to ensure proper receipt.
